title: Notice Lead and the Damages Portion of C&I Termination Security
content:
*Scope: Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts. Subject: termination security: notice lead.*

The termination security's damages portion is scaled by its notice lead, the calendar days from the termination notice date to the termination effective date: a lead of 75 days or more scales it by 0.80, a lead of 45 days up to 74 days scales it by 0.90, and a shorter lead leaves it unscaled. Scaling multiplies the damages portion by the figure shown.

The notice lead counts the days from the termination notice date to the termination effective date, the notice date itself not counted: a notice dated 2 March with an effective date of 16 May has a lead of 75 days.

## Schedule

| Notice lead in calendar days | Damages portion multiplied by |
|---|---|
| 75 or more | 0.80 |
| 45 to 74 | 0.90 |
| 44 or fewer | 1, unscaled |

## Boundary days

| Notice lead | Multiplier |
|---|---|
| 75 | 0.80 |
| 74 | 0.90 |
| 45 | 0.90 |
| 44 | 1 |

## Cases (hypothetical dates and amounts)

- Notice dated 2 March 2026, termination effective date 16 May 2026: lead 75 days; a damages portion of $10000.00 is taken at $8000.00.
- Notice dated 1 April 2026, termination effective date 5 May 2026: lead 34 days; the damages portion stays $10000.00.
